# Method notes

## The estimand: declare the target

| Target id | Weights |
|---|---|
| `V4-TARGET-RESPONDENT-WEIGHTED-v1` | every respondent equally |
| `V4-TARGET-EQUAL-CLUSTER-v1` | every cluster equally |

Under **informative cluster size** these are different population quantities.
`v4-estimand-and-sampling-contract-v1.yml` requires the target to be declared,
and every locked summary carries a `target` column so a number can never be
read without one.

In the SWMDK application the two differ by 0.0024 on the teacher scale
(0.6199 respondent-weighted, 0.6223 equal-cluster). Small — and reported
separately, because the difference is a property of the population rather than
noise to average away.

## What is conditioned on, and what is resampled

From the estimand contract:

| | |
|---|---|
| scale definition | **fixed** |
| observed cluster ids | **fixed** |
| observed cluster sizes | **conditioned** |
| random weights | a cluster-superpopulation posterior functional |

Cluster sizes are conditioned on, not resampled. That is a modelling choice
with consequences for what the interval covers, and it is written down rather
than left implicit.

## Exact H under arbitrary weights

The coefficient is computed by **finite comonotone transport** — exactly, under
whatever weights a bootstrap draw produces, rather than by an approximation
that happens to be close for equal weights.

::: {.callout-note}
## The transport result is not claimed as new

Claim CL-03 in the frozen register requires the predecessor credit to
**Andreadis (2017)** to be given, and the article never says "new transport
theorem". The contribution is the cluster-aware interval built on it, not the
transport identity.
:::

The independent [oracle lane](09-reproducibility.qmd#the-independent-oracle-lane)
checks the implementation against a linear-programming solution of the same
problem across an exhaustive grid: 32 configurations, 0 discrepancies.

## The two-stage bootstrap and why calibration *tightens*

Resample clusters, then respondents within clusters. Before calibration this is
**conservative** — the Phase 16 confirmation measured raw coverage at 99.75 %
(respondent) and 99.63 % (equal-cluster) against a nominal 95 %.

So the correction narrows rather than widens: a factor
k_G = 1 − 1.5/√G, which for the application's G = 30 gives **0.7261**.

::: {.callout-important}
This runs the **opposite way** from the companion binary paper, whose
calibration widens a slightly-short interval. Same idea — a measured correction
to a measured miss — in opposite directions, because the two procedures err in
opposite directions.

`verify_semantics.R` asserts the direction (`p16_sel_raw_ratio < 1`), and one
of the negative controls flips it to confirm the check bites.
:::

After calibration: 97.36 % and 97.38 % coverage, at about 75 % of the raw
length. Still conservative relative to 95 %, and the paper says so rather than
presenting it as exact.

## Exact knots are disclosures, not errors

The transport path reports **exact-knot counts** — configurations where a
marginal CDF gap is exactly zero. The article reports these as *diagnostic
disclosures of the weighted-marginal transport path, not error flags*, and the
application had 2 on the teacher respondent-weighted lane and 0 on the
equal-cluster lane.

They matter for reading [the archival
defect](09-reproducibility.qmd#the-archival-defect): the corrected kernel
advances on exact zero by design, so an exact knot is a handled case rather
than a risk.

## The claim boundary

Six phrases the article never asserts outside a negation:

> "first-ever" · "universally superior" · "new transport theorem" ·
> "credible interval" · "posterior probabilit…" · "analytically derived"

The interval is a **confidence interval**. The hierarchical Bayesian bootstrap
is a resampling device, and the property claimed is repeated-sampling coverage.

A **frozen claim-eligibility register** of 14 claims, written at the
source-review gate, governs the article's wording. It ships as Table H1;
`verify_semantics.R` asserts all 14 are transcribed into it.
